subject.title: Plugin installs crash Express 4.x routes: core npm-shrinkwrap pins path-to-regexp@8.x but no central override covers plugins

question: Should managed npm plugin roots inherit all host workspace overrides, or should OpenClaw scope/filter overrides such as path-to-regexp when they conflict with a plugin-owned dependency graph?
rationale: Both choices affect plugin dependency ownership and security override policy, so automation should not choose the permanent boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Scope managed-root overrides
options.body: Filter or condition host overrides so plugin-owned Express 4 dependency graphs can resolve path-to-regexp 0.1.x while core keeps Express 5/router on 8.x, then add regression coverage.

options.title: Add validator only
options.body: Keep current override propagation but fail or warn clearly for Express 4 plugins that lack their own package override, accepting that plugin authors must repair their packages.

options.title: Require plugin-owned fix
options.body: Treat this as external plugin packaging responsibility and leave OpenClaw behavior unchanged, pointing affected plugins to add an override or move to Express 5.

recommendation.title: Scope managed-root overrides
recommendation.body: Filter or condition host overrides so plugin-owned Express 4 dependency graphs can resolve path-to-regexp 0.1.x while core keeps Express 5/router on 8.x, then add regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice centers on the managed npm-root override reconciliation area that amknight most recently changed.
